Explanation:

Because the eight friends’ available meeting windows (with minimum durations) and the inter‐neighborhood travel times make it impossible to “squeeze” all eight meetings into the afternoon period (which extends roughly from the earliest start of 13:45 up to Matthew’s end time at 21:00), we explored various orders. (Notice that some friends have short meetings while others require 90 minutes; also several “late‐afternoon” friends – for example Mark and Emily – would overlap in a way that travel would force one to be skipped.) 

One schedule that meets as many friends as possible (five friends total) is as follows:
• Begin by traveling from Chinatown (arriving by 13:45 at Golden Gate Park) to meet Melissa from 13:45 to 15:15 (her minimum 90 minutes fits inside her 13:45–17:30 window).
• Then drive from Golden Gate Park to Pacific Heights (a 16‑minute ride) to meet Mark from 15:31 to 16:16 (45 minutes, within his 15:00–17:00 window).
• Next, transfer to Fisherman’s Wharf (a 13‑minute trip from Pacific Heights) to meet Margaret from 16:29 to 16:44 (15 minutes; her window is very flexible, 14:45–20:15).
• Then, move on (an 8‑minute trip) to Embarcadero to meet Richard from 16:52 to 18:22 (90 minutes; his window is 15:15–18:45).
• Finally, travel (another 8‑minute ride) to Russian Hill and meet Matthew from 18:30 to 20:00 (90 minutes; his window is 17:30–21:00).

This itinerary was chosen after considering alternatives (for example ones including Rebecca, Emily or George) but the long 90‑minute meetings and the necessary travel between neighborhoods force trade‑offs so that the maximum count achievable is meeting five friends in a continuous afternoon schedule.

You can use this JSON schedule as the “best‐found” solution optimizing your goal of meeting as many friends as possible under the constraints.
